questions.question: If tan A = 3/7, then what is the value of cosec A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

tan A = 3/7

**Concept Used:**

Trigonometric identity: cosec² A = 1 + cot² A

**Calculation:**

⇒ cot A = 7/3 (since cot A = 1/tan A)

⇒ cosec² A = 1 + (7/3)²

⇒ cosec² A = 1 + 49/9

⇒ cosec² A = 58/9

⇒ cosec A = √(58/9) = √(58) / 3

**Hence, cosec A = √(58) / 3**

questions.question: A 1800 metres long train crosses a man walking in opposite direction in 10 seconds. If the speed of train is 8 times to the speed of man, then what is the speed of train?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Length of train = 1800 meters,

Time taken = 10 seconds,

Ratio of speeds = 8:1

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Total speed = Distance / Time = 1800 m / 10 s = 180 m/s (This is the relative speed)

Speed of train = 8/9 × total speed = 8/9 × 180 = 160 m/s

In km/hr, 160 × 18/5 = 576 km/hr

**Therefore the speed of the train is 576 km/hr.**

questions.question: Distance of a chord RS from the centre is 20 cm. If the length of this chord is 30 cm, then what will be the diameter of this circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **perpendicular** from the center bisects the **chord**, so half-chord = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

Using **Pythagorean Triplet** (15, 20, 25), the **radius** is 25 cm.

**Diameter** = 2 × **Radius** = 2 × 25 = 50 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Distance** of chord (d) = 20 cm, **Length of chord** (c) = 30 cm.

**Formula Used:** **Radius** (r) = √[d² + (c/2)²]; **Diameter** (D) = 2 × r.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f9011417471d6db380b36ff21b971f0ac0cc92604c0b8509aa20dd9adf9f60b.png] 

⇒ **Half-chord length** (MS) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ In **right-angled triangle** OMS, OM² + MS² = OS²

⇒ 20² + 15² = **Radius**²

⇒ 400 + 225 = **Radius**²

⇒ **Radius**² = 625

⇒ **Radius** = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ **Diameter** = 2 × 25 = 50 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chord Perpendicular Property

A **perpendicular** drawn from the center of a circle to a **chord** always bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem

For any **right-angled triangle**, the square of the **hypotenuse** (radius) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides (distance and half-chord).

Circle Diameter

The **diameter** is defined as the longest chord passing through the **center**, and its length is exactly **twice** the radius.</p

Rs. 43,120 is divided among P, Q and R such that P's share is 4/7 of total share of Q and R together and Q's share is 2/5 of total share of P and R together. What is the share of R?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **P : (Q + R)** = 4 : 7 (Total 11) and **Q : (P + R)** = 2 : 5 (Total 7).

To equate the total sum, multiply first ratio by 7 and second by 11 (LCM of 11, 7 is 77).

New ratios: **P** = 4 × 7 = 28 units, **Q** = 2 × 11 = 22 units.

**R's share** = Total − (P + Q) = 77 − (28 + 22) = 27 units.

Value of 27 units = (43120 ÷ 77) × 27 = 560 × 27 = 15120.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total Amount** = ₹43,120

**P's share** = 4/7 of (Q + R)

**Q's share** = 2/5 of (P + R)

**Formula Used:**

Individual Share = (Individual Ratio Part ÷ Total Ratio Parts) × Total Amount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc918a6d412c6c5a4410a0c05047ce8b6285371b3ca5e7d7ebe280dfa8d66230.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ P : (Q + R) = 4 : 7 ⇒ P : (P + Q + R) = 4 : 11

⇒ Q : (P + R) = 2 : 5 ⇒ Q : (P + Q + R) = 2 : 7

⇒ Total Ratio Parts = LCM of 11 and 7 = 77

⇒ P's units = (4 ÷ 11) × 77 = 28 units

⇒ Q's units = (2 ÷ 7) × 77 = 22 units

⇒ R's units = 77 − (28 + 22) = 27 units

⇒ 77 units = ₹43120

⇒ 1 unit = 43120 ÷ 77 = ₹560

⇒ Share of **R** = 27 × 560 = ₹15120

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15120.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Normalization

When comparing parts to a common total, the sum of the ratio terms for each subset must be scaled to the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual sums.

Proportional Division

If a sum S is divided in the ratio a : b : c, then the shares are (a/k)S, (b/k)S, and (c/k)S, where k = a + b + c.

Base Change in Ratios

P/(Q+R) = 4/7 implies P/(P+Q+R) = 4/(4+7) = 4/11. This conversion allows for direct comparison with the total amount.

questions.question: Three metallic cubes whose sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm respectively are melted and converted into a single cube. If there is no loss of metal in this process, then what is the length of the side of the new cube?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The total **volume** remains constant during the melting process.

Volume of new cube = 6³ + 8³ + 10³

Volume = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728 cm³

Side of new cube = √³(1728) = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides of three metallic cubes are **s₁ = 6 cm**, **s₂ = 8 cm**, and **s₃ = 10 cm**.

**Formula Used:** Volume of a cube = (side)³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e637c7543a8209291bd0e3370b29b1e901b2919f7bb29bb5bae89630ba8b393.png] 

⇒ Volume of 1st cube = 6³ = 216 cm³

⇒ Volume of 2ⁿd cube = 8³ = 512 cm³

⇒ Volume of 3rd cube = 10³ = 1000 cm³

⇒ Total volume of melted metal = 216 + 512 + 1000 = 1728 cm³

⇒ Let **'a'** be the side of the **new cube**.

⇒ a³ = 1728

⇒ a = √³(1728)

⇒ a = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of a Cube

For a cube with side 'a', the **Volume** is a³ and the **Total Surface Area** is 6a².

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cube of side 'a' is given by the **Diagonal** formula: d = a√3.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical faces of a cube (excluding top and bottom) is called the **Lateral Surface Area**, which is 4a².</p

questions.question: The average of marks obtained by X and Y is 35 less than the average marks obtained by Y and Z. If the marks obtained by Z is 85, what is the marks obtained by X?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average(Y,Z) - Average(X,Y) = 35,

Z = 85

**Concept Used:** 

Average formula, X+Y = 2(Average of X,Y) and Y+Z = 2(Average of Y,Z)

**Calculation:**

Average(Y,Z) - Average(X,Y) = 35,

⇒ (Y + Z)/2 - (X + Y)/2 = 35

⇒ Y + Z - X - Y = 70

⇒ 85 - X = 70

⇒ X = 15

**Therefore, the marks obtained by X are 15.**

questions.question: P sells a bottle to Q at a profit of 30 percent and Q sells it to R at a profit of 20 percent. What is the ratio of cost prices of P and R?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit percentages = 30%, 20%

**Concept Used:**

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP of Q = 130% of CP of P

⇒ CP of R = 120% of CP of Q

⇒ 120% of 130% of CP of P = 156% of CP of P

⇒ Ratio of CPs of P and R = CP of P/CP of R

⇒ 1/1.56 = 100/156 = 25 : 39

**Hence, the ratio of the cost prices of P and R is 25 : 39.**

questions.question: A man borrows a sum of Rs. 12,000 which amounts to Rs. 13,200 in 2 years on simple interest. What would have been the amount if the rate of interest was doubled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the rate of interest when Principal and Time are constant.

Original Simple Interest = Rs. 13,200 − Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

If the rate of interest is doubled, the Simple Interest will also be doubled.

New Simple Interest = 2 × 1,200 = Rs. 2,400

New Amount = Principal + New Interest = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Amount in 2 years (A) = Rs. 13,200

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = A − P

I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da3a82cf7318b08ad6307d87c03469ea7a1bef468aa7f1c8d3155d0f1097ca39.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original Interest = 13,200 − 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

⇒ 1,200 = (12,000 × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,200 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 1,200 ÷ 240 = 5%

⇒ New Rate = 2 × 5% = 10%

⇒ New Interest = (12,000 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100 = Rs. 2,400

⇒ New Amount = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal (P), Rate (R), and Time (T). If any one of these is multiplied by a factor while the others remain constant, the Simple Interest is simply multiplied by the same factor.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the original principal every year, meaning it remains constant per period. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the original principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Simple Interest Formula

The formula to calculate simple interest is I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. The total amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + I.
</p

questions.question: What is the value of (tan theta - sec theta + 1)/(tan theta + sec theta - 1)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let θ = 45°

Expression = (tan 45° − sec 45° + 1) / (tan 45° + sec 45° − 1) = (1 − √2 + 1) / (1 + √2 − 1)

⇒ Expression = (2 − √2) / √2 = √2 − 1

Check Option 4: cos 45° / (1 + sin 45°) = (1/√2) / (1 + 1/√2) = 1 / (√2 + 1) = √2 − 1

**∴ The correct answer is cos θ / (1 + sin θ).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (tan θ − sec θ + 1) / (tan θ + sec θ − 1)

**Formula Used:**

sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Replace 1 in the numerator with (sec² θ − tan² θ)

⇒ Numerator = tan θ − sec θ + (sec² θ − tan² θ)

⇒ Numerator = −(sec θ − tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ)

⇒ Numerator = (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ − 1)

⇒ Expression = [(sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ − 1)] / (tan θ + sec θ − 1)

⇒ Expression = sec θ − tan θ = (1 / cos θ) − (sin θ / cos θ)

⇒ Expression = (1 − sin θ) / cos θ

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin θ)

⇒ Expression = [(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ Expression = (1 − sin² θ) / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)] = cos² θ / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ Expression = cos θ / (1 + sin θ)

**∴ The correct answer is cos θ / (1 + sin θ).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The Pythagorean identities are sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Value Substitution Method

When simplifying trigonometric expressions, substituting standard angles (like 30°, 45°, or 60°) can quickly verify the correct option. Always ensure the substituted angle doesn't make any denominator zero.

Conjugate Properties

Multiplying and dividing by the conjugate (e.g., 1 + sin θ) helps rationalize terms, allowing seamless conversions like (1 − sin θ) / cos θ → cos θ / (1 + sin θ).
</p

Raman spends 50 percent of his income. If his income increases by 10 percent and the expenditure also increases by 10 percent, then what will be the percentage increase in his savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the percentage increase in **Income** and **Expenditure** is exactly the same, the percentage increase in **Savings** will also be the same value.

Given: **Income** increase = 10% and **Expenditure** increase = 10%.

By property: % change in **Savings** = % change in **Income** = % change in **Expenditure**.

∴ **Percentage increase** in savings = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial expenditure = 50% of **Income**

Increase in **Income** = 10%

Increase in **Expenditure** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

**Percentage Increase** = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/544ed8ca9510179151f59e4a05dcafc0cd5ec1a3b7acebc21ac4ed8343ed7393.png] 

Let initial **Income** = 100

⇒ Initial **Expenditure** = 50% of 100 = 50

⇒ Initial **Savings** = 100 − 50 = 50

⇒ New **Income** = 100 + 10% of 100 = 110

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 50 + 10% of 50 = 50 + 5 = 55

⇒ New **Savings** = 110 − 55 = 55

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 55 − 50 = 5

⇒ **Percentage Increase** in Savings = (5 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ **Percentage Increase** in Savings = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The basic relationship is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in one component affects the others if total income is not constant.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is calculated as: [(Change in value) ÷ (Original value)] × 100.

Effect of Uniform Percentage Change

If every component of a linear sum (like A = B + C) increases by the same percentage k%, then the total sum A also increases by exactly k%.</p

questions.question: Two identical circles intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of common chord is 16sqrt{3} cm. What is the radius of each circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
When two **identical circles** pass through each other's **centers**, the length of the **common chord** is given by **r√3**.

Given: Common chord = 16√3 cm

⇒ r√3 = 16√3

⇒ r = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Two circles are **identical**, so Radius **r₁ = r₂ = R**.

⇒ Each passes through the center of the other, so **distance between centers (d) = R**.

⇒ Length of **common chord (L)** = 16√3 cm.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/334201cd6fbc3e23ef1d48a22757b77d2966f638fb404a8e05b7b89e270f1597.png] 
**Property:** When two identical circles of radius **R** pass through each other's centers, the **line of centers** (O₁O₂) and the **common chord** (AC) bisect each other at **right angles**.

⇒ Let **M** be the midpoint of **O₁O₂**.

⇒ O₁M = R / 2

⇒ In right-angled triangle **ΔO₁MA**, by **Pythagoras Theorem**:

⇒ AM² = O₁A² − O₁M²

⇒ AM² = R² − (R / 2)²

⇒ AM² = R² − R² / 4 = 3R² / 4

⇒ AM = (R√3) / 2

⇒ Length of **common chord (AC)** = 2 × AM = R√3

⇒ Given AC = 16√3 cm

⇒ R√3 = 16√3

⇒ R = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Chord of Two Intersecting Circles

Length = 2 × √(R² − d₁²), where d₁ is the distance from the center to the chord.

Distance between centers

For identical circles passing through centers, the distance d = R. If they touch externally, d = 2R. If they touch internally, d = 0.

Area of Intersection

The overlapping area of two identical circles passing through each other's centers is given by R²(2π/3 − √3/2).</p

questions.question: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn Rs. 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Wage ratio = Inverse ratio of days taken = 1/10 : 1/20 : 1/30 = 6 : 3 : 2

Total ratio parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts → Rs. 1100

1 part → Rs. 100

Required difference = (A + C) − B = (6 + 2) − 3 = 5 parts

Difference = 5 × 100 = Rs. 500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 10 days

Time taken by B alone = 20 days

Time taken by C alone = 30 days

Total earnings = Rs. 1100

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 10
 60
 6
 
 

 B
 20
 3
 
 

 C
 30
 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of efficiencies A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2

⇒ Total efficiency parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts

⇒ Earnings of A = (6 ÷ 11) × 1100 = Rs. 600

⇒ Earnings of B = (3 ÷ 11) × 1100 = Rs. 300

⇒ Earnings of C = (2 ÷ 11) × 1100 = Rs. 200

⇒ Total earnings of A and C = 600 + 200 = Rs. 800

⇒ Required difference = Total earnings of (A + C) − Earnings of B

⇒ Required difference = 800 − 300 = Rs. 500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If individuals work together for the same number of days, their wages are divided exactly in the ratio of their one-day work (efficiencies).

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. For instance, if the ratio of time taken by two people is A : B, their efficiency ratio is B : A.

Total Work Assumption

A highly effective way to determine total work is by calculating the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the distinct days taken by all individuals to finish the task alone.
</p

What is the value of central angle formed by sector F?
questions.solution:

Percentage of total number of girls in sector F = 17%

The value of central angle formed by sector F = 360/100 × 17 = 61.2°

questions.question: Which of the following is largest among (125)^(1)/(6), (11)^(1)/(3), (12)^(1)/(6), (5)^(1)/(4) ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of denominators of powers (6, 3, 6, 4) is 12.

Raise all values to the 12th power:

((125)¹/⁶)¹² = 125² = 15625

((11)¹/³)¹² = 11⁴ = 14641

((12)¹/⁶)¹² = 12² = 144; ((5)¹/⁴)¹² = 5³ = 125

Comparing results: 15625 > 14641 > 144 > 125.

**∴ The correct answer is (125)¹/⁶.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (125)¹/⁶, (11)¹/³, (12)¹/⁶, (5)¹/⁴

**Formula:** To compare a¹/ⁿ and b¹/m, convert them to a common index by finding the LCM of denominators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71aad04defbc2e72676231319f02ac3f5b8e8d7a39beebd013a19c1fbbe61805.png] 

⇒ Convert all powers to a common denominator 12:

⇒ (125)¹/⁶ = (125)²/¹² = (125²)¹/¹² = (15625)¹/¹²

⇒ (11)¹/³ = (11)⁴/¹² = (11⁴)¹/¹² = (14641)¹/¹²

⇒ (12)¹/⁶ = (12)²/¹² = (12²)¹/¹² = (144)¹/¹²

⇒ (5)¹/⁴ = (5)³/¹² = (5³)¹/¹² = (125)¹/¹²

⇒ Since 15625 > 14641 > 144 > 125, the largest value is (15625)¹/¹².

**∴ The correct answer is (125)¹/⁶.**

**__Additional Information__**

Comparing Surds of Different Indices

To compare numbers like ⁿ√a and m√b, find the LCM of n and m. Raise both numbers to the power of the LCM to eliminate the radical signs.

Laws of Indices

Important properties include (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ and a¹/ⁿ = ⁿ√a. These are essential for simplifying expressions before comparison.

Ascending and Descending Order

Once terms are converted to the same index (e.g., x¹/¹²), they can be sorted based on the magnitude of the base x.</p

questions.question: If a + (1)/(a) = 4, then what is the value of a⁴ + (1)/(a⁴)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a + 1/a = 4

**Formula used:**

If a + 1/a = k, then

a² + 1/a² = k² - 2

a4 + 1/a4 = (k2 - 2)² - 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ a4 + 1/a4 = (42 - 2)2 - 2

⇒ a4 + 1/a4 = (16 - 2)2 - 2

⇒ a4 + 1/a4 = (14)2 - 2 = 194

**Hence, the value of a⁴ + 1/a⁴ is 194.**
